generalCriterionList.description: Tenders  from Joint ventures are not acceptable.

Bidders shall not be under a declaration of ineligibility for
 corrupt and fraudulent practices issued by Government of Karnataka
Bidders shall ensure upload of relevant documents.

It shall be the responsibility of the Bidder to ensure credit of Tender Processing Fee and EMD into the respective receiving bank accounts of e-Procurement on or before the last date and time of bid submission.
EMD Payments through e-Payment mode shall be made as one single transaction and payments made in part are liable for rejection.

The bidder is required to ensure browser compatibility of the computer well in advance to the last date and time for receipt of tenders. The departments shall not be responsible for non accessibility of e Procurement portal due to internet connectivity issues and technical glitches at bidders end

Bidder shall pay Contract Management Module processing fees of 0.025% of the contact value (Min Rs.500/- & Max Rs.7500/-) soon after contract has been issued to bidder and as per prevailing Govt orders
Conditional tenders will not be accepted.
The tenderer shall bear all costs associated with the preparation and submission of his tender, and the employer will in no case be responsible and liable for those costs.
The cost of the Tender processing fee shall not be refundable.
The employer is not responsible for any delay in accessing Karnataka Public Procurement Portal.
Contractors Should be registered with KPWD as Class-II and above.(valid license)
Royalty on construction materials and other taxes will be deducted as per prevailing Govt orders.
All scanned documents to be uploaded shall be in original and the Executive Engineer reserves the right to verify the documents before approval.
The employer reserves the rights to Reject or accept any or all the tenders without assigning any reasons.
The intending contractors are requested to note that they should abide by the detailed instructions and conditions contained in the Standard Tender documents KW-4 and further orders thereon.

In the case of the death of the contractor after executing the agreement / commencement of the work, his legal heir, if is an eligible registered contractor and is willing can execute and complete the work at the accepted tender rates irrespective of the cost of the work

Contractor should take all precautions to ensure that no damage is caused to any adjacent structures/utilities above or below the ground and also to the existing canal CD works and other similar structures which have been constructed by other agencies during project execution. If any damage is caused, it has to be rectified at his own risk and cost. Damage to physical property and personal injury and death will be the personal risk of the contractor.

All safety precautions, warning signs, night illumination, reflectors, deployment of security guards has to be ensured so that no untoward incident happens on account of negligence or any project activity. Contractor should indemnify the client to that extent.
Formation levels and other data furnished are bare minimum the contractor should make all efforts to validate and to get additional data if required at his own cost
Contractor should execute the project with least impact to the environment till the completion of project.

All materials required for the work like bitumen, steel, cement etc., shall be procured by the tenderer themselves and should got tested by the quality control authority before use on the work at their own cost.

All the items in the tender including all lead, lifts,loading unloading, transportation, labour, hire charges of machinery curing for concrete works, cost and convence of all matiral and all other such incidental charges necessary for successful completion of works as per the detalied technical specification and direction of Engineer-in-charge of this work.

When embankments are constructed disputes arising on account of damages to the existing field channels, bunds and other private properties, if any, has to be resolved by the contractor. All precautions should be taken by the contractor so that there are no damages to such public/ private properties.
Contractor should follow strictly the privaling rules of labour act & The contractor should employ only registered labours as per Govt. Circular No. PWD/198/BMS/2009/ Dated: 24-06-2009

As per the Government Circular No.PWD:ITC:2008/2099, Dated.2-12-2010, the tendered contractors, should submit the Original Bank Guarantee issued by the Bankers for the said work at the time of opening of the Technical Bids. The Contractors failing to submit the Original Bank Guarantees will be disqualified and the initial amount deposited through E-payment will be forfeited and also such contractors will be Black listed and Debarred from participating in future tenders.

Royalty on construction materials and other taxes will be deducted as per prevailing Govt. orders. As per Karnataka state Government order LD/300/LET/2006 Bangalore dated 01.01.2007 and Government letter no PW/134/BMS/2007 dated 27.07.2007, a sum amounting to 1% of the bill amount will be deducted towards constructions labour welfare fund.

Minimum One Lakh Rupees of the specified EMD should be paid in any one of the forms mentioned in Clause 13.1, Bank Guarantee must be given for the remaining amount in prescribed format. The copy of the Bank Guarantee must be scanned and submitted along with the Technical bid. The original should be produced during opening of Technical bid
The successful tenderer should provide monthly physical and financial progress to be achieved in Bar chart/Milestone chart/PERT chart during agreement.
The returns submitted to the I.T. along with the Profit and Loss account statement,Balance sheet should be uploaded for the financial turnover criteria attested by registered Chartered Accountant.
GST is not included in the rates.

Regarding Appealing aggrieved contractors may appeal to the prescribed (Appellant) authority within 15 days as per KTTP and appeal should be through KPPP only as per Govt.order No:pwd/572/CRM-2020(E) Bangalore DT.09-10-2020. The same will not be considered if appeal through Letters.
Eighteen Percent GST shall be paid to the tendered amount separately.
The defect liability period for this project shall be 2 Years (Initial 2 years DLP without any financial implications and subsequent 3 years DLP nominal maintenance should be carried out as per BOQ
The successful contractor should setup material testing laboratory at the work site before commencement of work

Contractor should adhere to HSE (Health Safety Environment) policy applicable for similar projects. Contractor to that extentshould submit HSE document defining all the procedure including the policies before execution of the project

The safety precautions, warning signs, night illumination, reflectors, deployment of security guards has to be ensured so that no untoward incident happens on account of negligence or any project activity. Contractor should indemnify the client to that extent.
The success-full contractor should complete the whole work with in 4 months from the date of handing over of site (including rainy season)

Embankment/Subgrade : 5702 Cum 2. GSB : 1459 Cum 3. WMM : 1645 Cum 4.DBM/SDBC/BC/CC/MSS : 441 Cum 5. PCC/RCC : 395 Cum 6. Steel : 18.10 MT

3.5 Tenderers who meet the above specified minimum qualifying criteria, will only be qualified, if their available tender capacity is more than the total tender value. The available tender capacity will be calculated as under, Assessed available tender capacity (AxNx1.5 - B) where. A is Maximum value of civil engineering works executed in any one year during the last five years (updated to 2026-27 price level) taking into account the completed as well as works in progress. N is Number of years prescribed for completion of the works for which tenders are invited. B is Value, at 2026-27 price level, of existing commitments and on-going works to be completed during the next 4 months (period of completion of the works for which Tenders are invited)
